notes.b1/j1/F-r1: Clean empty 32x32 sandbox with four kinds, per-stroke undo, confirm-to-clear, live counts and a good phone layout, but only four plain blocks and an empty start make it less delightful.
notes.b1/j1/Q-r1: Richest and most polished: textured pixel blocks, sky, trees and pond in a ready seeded world, nine blocks, undo, new world, clear, hover ghost and persistence, all working on desktop and mobile.
notes.b1/j1/A-r1: Functional with Place/Erase/Pick/Fill tools and a pre-built ground layer, but the tiny key-number labels are barely legible, the blocks are flat and a full-width ground slab fills the world.
notes.b1/j1/Q-r2: Seeded little scene with ten block types, working erase tool, Shift/right-click break, Ctrl+Z, cell readout and persistence; blocks are simpler than V but the whole thing is solid and responsive.
notes.b1/j1/A-r2: Works as a basic painter with eight blocks, erase, grid toggle and a generate button, but it starts as a nearly black empty canvas, looks flat, has stray grid artifacts, and its toolbar crowds the swatches with actions.
notes.b1/j1/F-r2: Tidy block box with per-kind counts, hover ghost, placement flash and good accessibility text, but only four kinds, an empty start, and Ctrl+Z does nothing even though bare Z undoes.
notes.b1/j2/Q-r2: Seeded 32x32 world with house, tree and pond, beveled blocks, ten-block palette, undo and saved state; sky is plain dark and swatches carry no names.
notes.b1/j2/A-r2: Works with erase, grid and generate buttons, but opens to a blank dark grid with flat tiles, an unlabeled toolbar and a hint that does not mention the Grid and Generate buttons.
notes.b1/j2/F-r2: Clean, accessible Block Box with counts, flash feedback, status messages and an 8-cell guide grid, though it has only four block kinds and starts empty.
notes.b1/j2/A-r1: Starts with a ground layer and adds pick and fill tools with ten blocks, but the swatches are unfocusable divs with no names, the status line is cluttered, and undo records empty actions.
notes.b1/j2/Q-r1: Most game-like: textured blocks over a sky with clouds, generated terrain with trees and water, line-interpolated drags, new-world and undo, and it fits desktop and phone well.
notes.b1/j2/F-r1: Polished and responsive with hi-DPI canvas, a two-step clear, pop animation and well-labeled kinds, but it opens empty with only four kinds.
notes.b1/j3/A-r2: Works with Erase, Grid, Undo, Generate and Clear, but opens as an empty dark grid with faint lines and low-contrast, flat blocks.
notes.b1/j3/F-r2: Clean, accessible, with per-kind counts, hover ghost, status text and large touch targets, but only 4 kinds and an empty start that feels bare.
notes.b1/j3/Q-r2: Pre-built scene with house, tree, pond and 9 beveled blocks plus erase, Undo, Clear and persistence; sky-less dark background keeps it a bit plain.
notes.b1/j3/F-r1: Polished with DPR-aware canvas, pop animation, confirm-to-clear and 8-cell guides, yet only 4 kinds and an empty start.
notes.b1/j3/A-r1: Pre-filled ground with 10 colors, Place, Erase, Pick, Fill, Grid and Undo tools gives the most functionality, though visuals are plain and some key labels are hard to read.
notes.b1/j3/Q-r1: Textured blocks, sky gradient, clouds, generated terrain with trees and water, line-interpolated drags, New world and Undo make it a charming, complete sandbox.
notes.b2/j1/F-r3: Top-down 32x32 with real column stacking (height cap 6), remove mode, undo, keyboard shortcuts, but only three block types, an empty start, and the mobile toolbar overflows.
notes.b2/j1/Q-r3: Side-view 32x32 world with a textured starter landscape, ten block types, drag painting with interpolation, undo, reset, autosave and a tidy mobile layout.
notes.b2/j1/A-r3: Plain flat-color DOM grid on a dark empty board with 8 types, undo and autosave; functional but bare and the board reads as dark and lifeless.
notes.b2/j1/Q-r4: Isometric 32x32 voxel world with stackable blocks, shaded faces, translucent water and glass, starter terrain, place/erase modes, picking and undo; the strongest block-building feel, though redraws are heavy and the mobile view is small.
notes.b2/j1/A-r4: Flat top-down painter with 8 types, undo, PNG save and autosave; the grid lines render unevenly on mobile and there is no height.
notes.b2/j1/F-r4: Polished and accessible flat grid with counts, status messages, a two-step clear and focus states, but only four block types, an empty start, and the status and help text fall below the fold on desktop.
notes.b2/j2/Q-r4: True isometric 3D voxel world on a 32x32 grid with stacked heights, nine block types, place/erase, undo, hover ghost, starter terrain and saving; reads as a real block game, though the canvas is small on phones.
notes.b2/j2/A-r4: Flat 2D painter with eight colours and PNG save, but it starts empty, has no stacking, and its mobile grid lines are uneven.
notes.b2/j2/F-r4: Clean and well labelled with a counter, undo and keyboard picks, but it is just four block types painted flat on a blank grid with no depth, and the first screen shows nothing built.
notes.b2/j2/A-r3: Flat div grid with nine types and a side panel, but it is dark and empty with faint cells, and the mobile layout pushes the palette below the board.
notes.b2/j2/Q-r3: Minecraft-like side-view 32x32 world with textured blocks, sky, a tree and water, plus erase, undo and reset; it works well, though it is a 2D slice rather than a full world.
notes.b2/j2/F-r3: Top-down grid with stackable columns up to height 6, a clear-armed flow and good keyboard support, but only three block types and a subtle pseudo-height look; the mobile toolbar clips.
notes.b2/j3/A-r4: Working flat top-down painter with 8 colors, undo, save PNG, but blank and plain, and the mobile canvas grid renders with uneven moire lines.
notes.b2/j3/F-r4: Polished flat 32x32 painter with counts, disabled states, two-step clear and good a11y, but only 4 kinds and starts empty with little sense of building.
notes.b2/j3/Q-r4: Isometric 3D voxel world with stacking, terrain, pond and tree, picking, hotbar, undo, erase and persistence; clearly feels like a block-building sandbox and is responsive.
notes.b2/j3/F-r3: Top-down grid with stackable columns up to 6 and a fake-height look, clear controls and keyboard shortcuts, but only 3 block types and a dull empty start.
notes.b2/j3/A-r3: Plain dark DOM grid with a side palette; works and autosaves but is visually bland, empty at rest, and the mobile palette pushes controls below the fold.
notes.b2/j3/Q-r3: Side-view Minecraft-like world with textured blocks, prefilled terrain and tree, 9 block types, undo/clear/reset and persistence; charming and works well though canvas runs slightly below fold on desktop.
